explanations.answer: Not one stone will be left on another
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus asks, “Do you see all these things?” and then says, “…not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” His disciples, the men following Him, had come up to point out the buildings. I think that answer was not what they were expecting.

explanations.answer: Every stone will be covered in gold
explanations.explanation: Gold sounds fancy, but Jesus never says it. He says, “…not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” His disciples, the men following Him, were pointing out the buildings, and Jesus told them where those buildings were headed. No gold, no gift wrap, just that.

explanations.answer: Every stone will stand for all time
explanations.explanation: That's the opposite of what Jesus says. He tells them, “…not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” So the stones don't stand forever. I think the disciples were hoping for a different answer, because nobody points out buildings to hear that.

explanations.answer: When it will happen and what the sign will be
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker. The disciples say, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?” They come to Him privately to ask. Two questions in one breath, and I respect a person who stacks them up like that.

explanations.answer: Who will tear the temple down and how
explanations.explanation: Good guess, since Jesus just talked about stones being thrown down. But the disciples don't ask who or how. They ask, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?” They want the timing and the sign.

explanations.answer: Where they should go and who to bring
explanations.explanation: That sounds like a trip plan, and I love a good plan. But nobody asks about travel here. The disciples come to Jesus privately and ask, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?” It's all about timing and the sign.

You got it, baker. Jesus answers, “See to it that no one deceives you.” They asked about timing, and the very first thing out of His mouth is a warning. When the answer starts somewhere you didn't expect, pay attention.

Nope, no secret-keeping here. Even though the disciples came to Him privately, Jesus' first words are, “See to it that no one deceives you.” That's the warning He opens with. Nothing in this passage tells them to keep quiet.

explanations.answer: Don't go back to the temple
explanations.explanation: Jesus did just leave the temple, so I see the thinking. But He never says a word about going back or staying away. His first warning is, “See to it that no one deceives you.” It's about being deceived, not about where they walk.

Not quite, baker, and this one is easy to slide past. Jesus says, “For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many.” So it's many who come, and they deceive many. A few is nowhere in that verse.
That's right, baker. Jesus says, “For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many.” Many come and many get deceived. That's why His opening warning matters so much.

Yes, baker. Jesus says, “You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed.” He doesn't say the news will be light. He says not to be alarmed. You know when you refresh the news every ten seconds? That's a tall order for a lot of us.

explanations.answer: Get out of the city fast
explanations.explanation: Running sounds natural when the news gets scary. But Jesus doesn't tell them to flee here. He says, “…see to it that you are not alarmed.” The instruction is about not being alarmed.

Jesus doesn't send anybody to the battle here. He says, “You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed.” They hear about the wars, and He tells them not to be alarmed. No armor required.
That's the word, baker. Jesus says, “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” So the wars aren't the end. Hearing that, I'd say my shoulders just dropped an inch.
Peace would be nice, wouldn't it? But that's not the word Jesus uses. He says, “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” The word is end, and the wars aren't it yet.
Rest sounds lovely, baker. I have been known to want some myself. But Jesus says, “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” The word He uses is end.

That's the picture, baker. Jesus says, “All these are the beginning of birth pains.” After wars, famines and earthquakes, He calls them the beginning of something. One word in that verse matters a lot, and it's beginning.

A long winter does sound like a rough season. But it's not the picture Jesus picks. He says, “All these are the beginning of birth pains.” Wars, famines and earthquakes get called the beginning of birth pains.
A harvest is a nice image, but Jesus doesn't use it here. He says, “All these are the beginning of birth pains.” That's the picture He gives for the wars, famines and earthquakes.

You got it, baker. Jesus says, “Then they will deliver you over to be persecuted and killed, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.” I think this one is heavy, and it's okay to say so. It's also exactly what He tells them.

It's a hard one to believe, so no worries. But Jesus really does say it: “…you will be hated by all nations because of My name.” I think this part is heavy. It's right there in the text, and He says it out loud.

That's the word, baker. Jesus says, “Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.” Notice He says most. I'd rather my cookies cool than my love, so that's a sobering one.

I like the hope in that, but it's the opposite of the verse. Jesus says, “Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.” Wickedness multiplies and love grows cold. It's a hard line, but that's what He says.

Deep is a good word for love, but it isn't the one Jesus uses. He says, “Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.” When wickedness multiplies, love goes cold for most.
Yes, baker! Jesus says, “But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” After a verse about love growing cold, that line lands like the oven door opening in winter. Warm, and just in time.
I get it, since this whole list feels like a test. But Jesus doesn't use that word here. He says, “But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” The word is saved.
Sent is a decent guess, but that's not the word here. Jesus says, “But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” The one who perseveres gets saved. That's the word, and it's a good one.

Not this time, baker. Jesus says the gospel “…will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.” That's all the world and all nations. Israel only is much smaller than what He says.

That's right, baker. Jesus says, “And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.” All the world and all nations is far bigger than Israel alone. The good news goes out wide, and that's exactly what He says.
